layers.title: People the land could feed
layers.note: Calories per hectare × arable share × 60 % of it in fields × the share sown in a year (68 %, fitted to the Han census; all of it where a second crop fits) ÷ 1.1 million kcal a person needs a year. A ceiling, not a census.

layers.title: Staple crop
layers.note: The crop (or crop pair) that gives the most calories after seed; hatched where a second crop fits in the months the first leaves free. Where both grow, barley and millet feed about as many (millet is within 5 % on a quarter of the land); a hex's card lists every crop.

layers.title: Food per hectare
layers.note: Low-input yields of the period (grain ~1 t/ha, paddy ~1.8 t/ha, dates 3 t/ha), scaled by the season's water balance (FAO-33), net of seed.

layers.title: Growing season
layers.note: FAO length of growing period: months at or above 5 °C with rain plus soil water at least half the potential evaporation (Thornthwaite, 100 mm soil).

layers.title: Wild productivity
layers.note: Net primary productivity, Miami model (Lieth 1975): the lesser of the temperature and rain limits.

layers.title: Rain against evaporation
layers.note: Annual rain over Thornthwaite potential evaporation: under 0.2 desert, 0.2-0.5 steppe, 0.5-1 dry farming, over 1 humid.

layers.title: Irrigation reach
layers.note: Land watered from the rivers: exp(-d/6 km) from the navigable rivers, 0.6 exp(-d/2.5 km) from streams.

layers.title: Malaria climate
layers.note: MARA climatic suitability (Craig et al. 1999): five months running at 22-32 °C with 80 mm of rain or more (fuzzy edges).

Egypt.source: 1st-2nd c., with Alexandria: Bagnall & Frier 1994, Rathbone 1990, Frier 2000

North China Plain (Han Yan, Yu, Ji, Qing.source: AD 2 census (Hanshu 28): 29.4 M on 365,000 km²; areas Zheng & Wu 2026

Roman Italy (mainland).source: AD 14-165, low count (Beloch 1886, Frier 2000) to high (Lo Cascio 1994, Harper 2017)

Mesopotamian alluvium.source: Parthian to Sasanian peak: Adams 1965, 1981 (settled area, 100-200 per ha)
